takeaway: Inguinal canal: roof = arching fibres of internal oblique and transversus abdominis; anterior wall = external oblique (plus internal oblique laterally); posterior wall = transversalis fascia and conjoint tendon.

lines.text: Which structures form the roof of the inguinal canal?
The roof is made of arching muscle fibres.
The arching fibres of internal oblique,
Compare the other walls. The anterior wall is external oblique, with internal oblique for the lateral third.
The posterior wall is transversalis fascia and the conjoint tendon.
So the roof is internal oblique and transversus abdominis.
